memory_update.text: Technology theme should be researched as an AI/cloud infrastructure system rather than a single software or semiconductor ticker basket.
Advanced packaging, HBM backend, and OSAT/package-test capacity are priority Layer 1A chokepoint nodes for underfollowed discovery.
Semiconductor process control, inspection, metrology, and yield management are cross-cycle beneficiaries of rising AI chip and packaging complexity.
CPO and silicon-photonics upstream manufacturing stack should be searched through epitaxy, MOCVD, etch/deposition, bonding, substrates, and optical test rather than only switch ASICs.
Data-center power, cooling, and electrical balance-of-plant remain important infrastructure nodes, but underfollowed discovery should move below the obvious reference leaders.
Cloud security, machine identity, observability, and automation software form a lower-confidence but potentially underfollowed second-order software lane.
Next layer must verify company-level exposure using filings, earnings transcripts, customer evidence, backlog, segment revenue, market cap, analyst coverage, and valuation context.

summary: Layer 1A decomposes the broad Technology theme into six investable research nodes where AI/cloud/software demand may create second-order bottlenecks beyond obvious mega-cap beneficiaries. The strongest initial chokepoint candidates are: advanced packaging and HBM backend capacity; semiconductor process control and inspection; compound-semiconductor equipment for CPO/silicon photonics; data-center power and cooling infrastructure; grid/interconnection and power availability; and machine-identity/cybersecurity/automation software tied to expanding cloud infrastructure. Reference leaders such as NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, TSMC, ASML, Arista, Vertiv, Eaton, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta define the demand vector, but the Layer 1A funnel should deliberately hunt one or two steps upstream or sideways for underfollowed public suppliers, tools, test vendors, niche software platforms, component distributors, and certification-constrained infrastructure providers.

theme_map.public_market_search_strategy: Use a two-lane Serenity funnel. Lane 1 maps reference leaders to validate demand: AI accelerators, cloud capex, advanced foundry, networking, power, and data-center infrastructure. Lane 2 deliberately searches for underfollowed public companies one or two steps away from the obvious winners: OSATs, package/test equipment, inspection/metrology, compound-semiconductor equipment, optical connectivity suppliers, thermal/power components, grid-service subcontractors, machine-identity/security software, observability, industrial automation, and specialized distributors. Favor companies with direct exposure to qualification bottlenecks, long lead times, customer validation, narrow process know-how, or messy industry labels that screen poorly in generic AI/software/semiconductor baskets. This is research support only and does not imply buy/sell recommendations.
supply_side_constraints: Advanced foundry and packaging capacity concentrated around a small number of qualified suppliers
HBM and advanced memory supply likely constrained by producer capacity, packaging/test throughput, yield, and capital allocation
Process-control and inspection tools become more valuable as AI chips and packaging become denser and harder to manufacture
CPO and silicon-photonics scale-up depends on upstream epitaxy, substrates, plasma etch/deposition, bonding, test, and yield learning curves
Data-center deployment may be limited by electrical equipment lead times, cooling capacity, utility interconnection, permitting, and physical construction services
Cybersecurity and automation software may face customer-budget scrutiny, but infrastructure expansion creates durable operational complexity that must be managed
